about: Lifetime ISA rules for tools/build-lifetime-isa-pages.js, each quoted from GOV.UK's Lifetime ISA guide.

sources.title: Lifetime ISA: who can open one

limits.quote: You can put in up to £4,000 each year, until you’re 50. You must make your first payment into your ISA before you’re 40. The government will add a 25% bonus to your savings, up to a maximum of £1,000 per year. The Lifetime ISA limit of £4,000 counts towards your annual ISA limit . This is £20,000 for the 2026 to 2027 tax year.

open.quote: You must be 18 or over but under 40 to open a Lifetime ISA .

withdraw.quote: You can withdraw money from your ISA if you’re: buying your first home aged 60 or over terminally ill, with less than 12 months to live You’ll pay a withdrawal charge of 25% if you withdraw cash or assets for any other reason

home12.quote: you buy the property at least 12 months after you make your first payment into the Lifetime ISA

homePrice.quote: If the property costs more than £450,000, you’ll pay a 20% withdrawal charge. There’s no withdrawal charge for properties costing £450,000 and under.

sixty.quote: You can take your savings out of a Lifetime ISA when you’re 60 or over. You’ll pay a 25% charge if you withdraw money or transfer the Lifetime ISA to another type of ISA before 60.

whole.quote: If you wish to withdraw the entire pot, a 25% charge will apply to the total amount in your ISA , including the government bonus.

fifty.quote: When you turn 50, you will not be able to pay into your Lifetime ISA or earn the 25% bonus. Your account will stay open and your savings will still earn interest or investment returns.
